clinician.final_diagnosis: Cutaneous metastases (CM) originating from primary breast carcinoma
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 53-year-old woman presented with a 5-month history of bilateral axillary and trunk nodules alongside systemic symptoms including asthenia, anorexia, and significant weight loss. Clinical breast exam showed no palpable masses. Skin nodule biopsy revealed metastatic undifferentiated carcinoma. Immunohistochemical stains showed ER positivity in 50% of tumor cells and negativity for PR and HER2, consistent with breast carcinoma metastasis. Elevated tumor markers CA 15-3 (>500 U/mL) and CEA (6.37 ng/mL) alongside an elevated ESR further supported malignancy. Treatment was initiated with palbociclib and aromatase inhibitors. Although skin lesions initially resolved, tumor markers rose indicating progression. The patient ultimately died 7 months after diagnosis. Breast imaging or biopsy confirming the primary tumor and detailed clinical course documentation are not available in the provided reports.
